subject: Order Form: SLA, On-call Window & Credit Schedule
messages:
From: Tom Kirby <tom.kirby@skylinetech.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skylinetech.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form draft + SLA redlines

Aditya,

Thanks for sending the draft order form. We've reviewed and attached a marked-up PDF with a few areas we need clarified before procurement can move to signature. High level asks: 

- Uptime target: your standard enterprise SLA in the order form says 99.95% but the redlines we received were 99.9. We need explicit confirmation which will apply and whether there's a phased path to 99.95 after pilot.
- Service credits: the redline caps credits at 25% monthly. That feels low for us — can you explain rationale and whether you can move to a 40% cap or a stepped credit schedule?
- Response times (P1/P2): our SRE team expects P1 acknowledgement within 15 minutes and P1 mitigation within 1 hour. Your draft lists acknowledgement within 30 minutes.
- Maintenance windows: the marked-up doc proposes a 6-hour rolling maintenance window per month; we typically allow 4 hours. Also need blackout dates language and advance notice timing.

Attached: Skyline_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf (our redlines). Please loop in legal if you need to. We want to avoid extended round trips — ideally consolidate a clean order form we can sign.

Thanks,
Tom Kirby
Head of IT Procurement
Skyline Technologies

Attachments: Skyline_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tom Kirby <tom.kirby@skylinetech.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form draft + SLA redlines

Tom — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Appreciate the level of detail. I pulled together an initial counter-proposal so we can limit legal rounds: 

- Uptime target: Redwood standard enterprise offering is 99.95% for Dedicated/Private customers. For a pilot, we can commit to 99.9% for the first 90 days and automatically upgrade to 99.95% on the first post-pilot month provided the feature/traffic baseline is met. We'll document the upgrade criteria in the order form.

- Service credits: I'm open to a stepped credit schedule rather than a hard 25% cap. Attached is an SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx that outlines: 0% for <99.9, 10% for 99.9-99.7, 25% for 99.7-99.0, 50% for <99.0 with an annual cap of 50% as a safety valve. That said, I'll let legal weigh in on final cap language.

- Response times: We can shorten P1 acknowledgement to 15 minutes for customers on the enterprise plan if we include a documented on-call contact and an agreed escalation path. P1 mitigation window of 1 hour is aggressive but we can commit to an initial mitigation plan within 1 hour and continuous updates until resolution.

- Maintenance: We can target 4 hours monthly standard window. For scheduled maintenance requiring >4 hours we will provide advance notice and propose staggered blackouts — also propose a clause that urgent security patches may be applied with 72 hours notice.

Next steps: 
1) Soojin — can you convert the above into redline language (maintenance exclusions, credit cap, measurement window wording)?
2) Lauren — can you confirm the commercial impact if we move to the staged credit cap vs the flat 25%?
3) Tom — if the staged approach looks okay, I suggest we do one legal redline pass and then move to DocuSign.

I attached the SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx with an initial proposal. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: SLA-credit-matrix.xlsx
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Tom Kirby <tom.kirby@skylinetech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form draft + SLA redlines

Aditya / Tom — following up with formal legal redline guidance based on Aditya's notes. Inline summary below; I'll send a marked-up order form if we agree on these points.

1) Measurement & uptime definition
- Define measurement window: monthly UTC rolling window measured at the ingress point for account traffic. Exclude scheduled maintenance windows (see below).
- Clarify what constitutes "Unavailability" (e.g., inability to accept new requests, not rate-limited responses).

2) Service credits and cap
- Recommend a stepped credit matrix (as Aditya outlined) but propose absolute cap of 30% of monthly recurring charges to balance commercial risk. Rationale: broader cap hampers operational stability and sets an outsized expectation for zero-downtime.
- Add clause: credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for service unavailability. Credits are not transferable and will be applied to the next billing cycle. Credits expire 30 days after the triggering month if not claimed.

3) Response / On-call
- Agree to 15-minute acknowledgement for P1 provided customer maintains an on-call contact and a runbook is shared.
- Define P1/P2 thresholds in appendix. Require customer to provide a primary and secondary on-call contact.

4) Maintenance windows & blackouts
- Default scheduled maintenance: up to 4 hours per calendar month with 72 hours advance notice for non-critical changes.
- Critical security patches: Redwood may apply with 72 hours notice, with post-facto client notification if immediate action required.
- Add blackout dates clause: customer may request up to 12 blackout days per 12-month period for major events; Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate.

5) Evidence & measurement
- All service availability calculations based on server-side logs and metrics; client may request supporting logs for up to 30 days following an incident.

6) Misc
- Limit retroactive credit claims to 30 days after the incident discovery.
- Include a small print: changes to SLA for Dedicated/Private deployments require 30 days notice post-signature.

Please confirm if Skyline can accept the 30% cap; if not we'll need to escalate to commercial leadership. If accepted, I'll prepare a redline and include the appendix language for P1/P2 definitions and the on-call obligations.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form draft + SLA redlines

Aditya / Soojin — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the clear position. A few quick items from our side: 

- We can accept the staged uptime approach (99.9% pilot -> 99.95% post-pilot) provided the upgrade is automatic based on usage thresholds and not at Redwood discretion. Please include the specific metric/ping counts that will trigger the upgrade in the order form.
- Service credit cap: 30% is moving in the right direction but our finance team prefers 40% as a middle ground. Can Redwood confirm 40% is possible for this customer class? If not, we may need to escalate to procurement leadership for sign-off.
- P1 response: 15-minute acknowledgement is critical. We can provide the on-call contacts and runbook as requested. P1 mitigation updates every 30 minutes please.
- Maintenance blackout language: the 12 blackout days and 72-hour notice are acceptable; please add a clause that Redwood will provide a draft maintenance calendar 30 days ahead of major events (e.g., product launches).

If you can incorporate Tom's bullets into a single redline pass, we can route to our legal team. Assuming that goes well, we'll finalize in DocuSign.

I'll stand by for the redline PDF.

Best,
Tom Kirby
Head of IT Procurement
Skyline Technologies

Attachments: none
